title: Introduce token slab index and alert attenuator for long-tail noise
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Context: alert noise from long-tail token-cost spikes has been creating a high-volume of low-actionable incidents. Several customers reported alerts triggered by rare prompt shapes that skew token-cost percentiles for short windows. Motivation: provide an efficient, queryable aggregation that preserves per-token cost fidelity for high-volume prefixes while allowing alert systems to mute spurious long-tail signals. What this PR does: 1) Adds a new 'token slab index' that buckets token-cost contributions into fixed slabs (e.g. 1-4,5-8,9-16 tokens) and maintains per-route + per-model slab rollups. This is implemented as a compact in-memory aggregator with periodic checkpointing to the metrics store. 2) Introduces an 'alert attenuator' integration which consumes slab histograms to calculate an attenuation score (probabilistic dampening) used by the alerting pipeline to reduce noisy alerts coming from low-support slabs. 3) Adds a dashboard (token-slab-explorer) with drilldowns from slabs to sampled log anchors (queryable links to stored log snippets), enabling on-call to inspect representative examples for an attenuated alert. 4) Updates ingestion and query paths: ingest side emits slab proto, query layer exposes a slab_index SQL function for efficient aggregation. 5) Adds docs, examples, and unit + integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of slab aggregator (telemetry/ingest) - [x] Query surface (slab_index function) - [x] Alert attenuator rule and CI gate - [x] Dashboard JSON and UX review - [x] Sampling hooks for log anchoring - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and runbook snippets Roadmap notes: this is intentionally conservative (fixed slab boundaries) so we can iterate with production telemetry first. If adoption is strong we will add adaptive slab tuning and compression in a follow-up (ENG-7490).

notes_for_ops: Config knobs: telemetry.slab.enabled (default true), telemetry.slab.checkpoint_interval (default 60s), alerts.attenuator.enabled (default true), alerts.attenuator.min_support_threshold (default 25). If you see legitimate alerts attenuated, set alerts.attenuator.min_support_threshold=1 for the tenant and contact telemetry@redwood.ai.
